papers.title: Multi-Scale Finite Element Simulation Framework for Deformation and Damage of Large Structure Under Complex Loadings
papers.abstract: This paper establishes a multi-scale nested sub-modeling finite element simulation framework for the deformation and damage analysis of large-scale structures under complex loading conditions. By sequentially transferring displacement solutions from the global model to local sub-models, the framework enables progressive high-resolution analysis from the macroscopic scale (>10 m) down to the microscopic scale (~1 μm), thereby significantly improving solution accuracy in critical regions while maintaining computational efficiency. The proposed approach is validated on a shell structure subjected to hydrostatic pressure and on a plate with a central crack. The results show that the relative errors of stress and strain along specified paths in the shell structure are within 5%, while the relative errors of the stress intensity factor along the crack front in the cracked plate are also below 5%. Furthermore, the framework is integrated with the crystal plasticity finite element method, and a fatigue indicator parameter model based on the accumulated equivalent plastic strain is established to predict the shear fatigue life of Ti-6Al-4V ELI titanium alloy. The predicted fatigue lives are in good agreement with experimental data, with all errors below 10%. This study demonstrates that the proposed sub-modeling method can accurately transfer multi-scale mechanical responses and achieve localized refinement analysis of large-scale structures and can be effectively used for crystal plasticity simulations and fatigue life assessment.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文针对Ti-6Al-4V ELI的疲劳寿命预测建立了多尺度有限元框架，直接符合方向要求。
llm.why_not_core: No as-built mechanical property data reported; validation uses published experimental results.

summary_zh.motivation: 开发适用于大型结构复杂载荷下变形与损伤分析的多尺度仿真框架
summary_zh.method: 建立嵌套子模型有限元框架，从宏观至微观逐级传递位移解，结合晶体塑性方法和疲劳指示参数模型
summary_zh.result: 壳体和裂纹板应力应变误差小于5%，Ti-6Al-4V ELI剪切疲劳寿命预测误差低于10%
summary_zh.validation: 通过壳体静压实验和含裂纹板应力强度因子计算验证，并与Ti-6Al-4V ELI疲劳实验数据对比

summary_en.motivation: To develop a multi-scale simulation framework for deformation and damage analysis of large structures under complex loadings.
summary_en.method: A nested sub-modeling finite element framework is established, transferring displacement solutions from global to local scales, integrated with crystal plasticity and a fatigue indicator parameter model.
summary_en.result: Stress and strain errors in shell and cracked plate are within 5%, and predicted shear fatigue lives of Ti-6Al-4V ELI agree with experiments within 10% error.
summary_en.validation: Validated against hydrostatic pressure test of shell structure, stress intensity factor of cracked plate, and experimental fatigue data of Ti-6Al-4V ELI.

papers.title: Effect of open-loop and closed-loop in-situ process control on microstructure and mechanical properties of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文直接研究了L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V的工艺控制（开环与闭环）对微观结构和力学性能的影响，符合L1方向对机械性能的关注。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not explicitly address fatigue performance, but it is still relevant as it covers tensile properties and microstructure which are part of L1 focus.

summary_zh.motivation: 研究开环与闭环原位过程控制对L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V微观结构和力学性能的影响。
summary_zh.method: 对比开环和闭环两种控制策略，进行L-PBF成型，然后表征微观结构和力学性能。
summary_zh.result: 闭环控制能显著改善微观结构均匀性和力学性能（如强度、延展性）。
summary_zh.validation: 通过拉伸测试、硬度测试和显微组织观察进行实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: To investigate the effect of open-loop versus closed-loop in-situ process control on the microstructure and mechanical properties of L-PBF Ti-6Al-4V.
summary_en.method: Two control strategies were implemented during L-PBF, followed by microstructural characterization and mechanical testing (tensile and hardness).
summary_en.result: Closed-loop control improved microstructural homogeneity and enhanced mechanical properties including strength and ductility.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation through tensile tests, hardness measurements, and microscopy analysis.
